title: Cho-Gochujang Sweet-Tangy Chili Sauce
shortDescription: Gochujang is loosened with rice vinegar and rice syrup, then balanced with sugar, garlic, and sesame seeds for a glossy sweet-tart dipping and dressing sauce.
culturalContext: Cho-gochujang, often shortened to chogochujang, is a vinegar-brightened gochujang sauce served with foods including seafood and vegetables. Sweetness, acidity, garlic, and sesame vary; this draft is one practical ratio awaiting Korean review.
author: {{LEGAL_NAME}}
equipment: Small digital scale or measuring cups

instructions.heading: Check labels
instructions.action: Read the gochujang, vinegar, and rice-syrup labels for soy, wheat/gluten, alcohol, sesame, and other declared allergens.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Products are within date, properly stored, and match the intended unseasoned vinegar and plain rice syrup.
instructions.safetyNote: Gochujang formulations vary; never infer gluten-free or alcohol-free status from the product name alone.

instructions.heading: Loosen the gochujang
instructions.action: Whisk gochujang with half the vinegar until smooth before adding the remaining vinegar.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: No dense paste pockets remain and the sauce flows slowly from the whisk.
instructions.safetyNote: Use a clean bowl and whisk for this ready-to-eat sauce.

instructions.heading: Sweeten
instructions.action: Whisk in rice syrup and sugar until the sugar is fully dissolved.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sauce is glossy with no gritty sugar at the bottom.
instructions.safetyNote: Do not taste with a utensil that will return to the master batch.

instructions.heading: Finish
instructions.action: Stir in optional grated garlic and sesame seeds. Adjust consistency only after the test kitchen evaluates the locked ratio.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: The sauce is pourable but thick enough to coat a spoon.
instructions.safetyNote: Declare soy, possible wheat/gluten and alcohol, and optional sesame allergens.

instructions.heading: Rest cold
instructions.action: Transfer to a clean covered glass container and refrigerate for 20 minutes.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Sauce remains smooth and cohesive after chilling.
instructions.safetyNote: Refrigerate promptly, especially when fresh garlic is included.

instructions.heading: Portion for service
instructions.action: Spoon into individual dishes and keep the master container refrigerated, replenishing only with a clean spoon.
instructions.visualOrTactileCue: Table portions are shallow and the stored batch remains untouched.
instructions.safetyNote: Discard any portion contacted by raw seafood, raw meat, or used eating utensils.

grillSetup: No grill is used to make the sauce; position individual dishes outside the raw-food and heat zones and keep the master batch refrigerated.
visualDonenessCues: Sauce is glossy, pourable, and thick enough to coat a spoon
foodSafetyNotes: Check packaged ingredients for soy, wheat/gluten, alcohol, and sesame.
Use clean tools and avoid double-dipping into the master batch.
Refrigerate at or below 40°F / 4°C, particularly when garlic is included.
Use individual dishes to control raw-seafood and raw-meat cross-contact.
Discard contaminated or temperature-abused table portions.

allergens.crossContactWarning: Contains soy and may contain wheat/gluten or alcohol; optional sesame adds another major allergen. Verify labels and portion separately from raw seafood.

substitutions: Use only a verified gluten-free gochujang for a gluten-free adaptation.
Corn syrup may replace rice syrup at equal volume after taste testing.
Omit sesame seeds for a sesame-free version only after checking gochujang cross-contact.
ingredientSourcing: Choose gochujang after comparing heat, sweetness, sodium, and allergen labels.
Use unseasoned rice vinegar so the recipe controls salt and sugar.
makeAhead: Make up to 1 day ahead and refrigerate; whisk before portioning.
storage: Refrigerate in a clean airtight container at or below 40°F / 4°C and use within 7 days; this conservative draft limit requires food-safety review.
reheating: Do not heat; serve cold or cool.
leftovers: Save only untouched sauce from the clean master container; discard all individual table portions after service.
servingSuggestions: Serve with chilled cooked seafood or blanched vegetables
Use sparingly as a sweet-tangy dressing

faq.question: What does cho add to gochujang?
faq.answer: The vinegar component brightens and loosens the fermented chile paste, creating a tangy dipping consistency.

faq.question: Can the sauce touch raw seafood?
faq.answer: Only a separate disposable portion should contact raw food; never return it to the refrigerated master batch.
